what: This run is a stand-in that proves the machinery. No training vectors were published when it ran, so two thirds of the `val` photos were used to fit the heads and the last third to choose settings. With about two fitting photos a species, these numbers say little about what the real training set (up to sixty photos a species) will give. They are here to show that every step runs and to be replaced.

The wildlife records hold no people and no photos with nothing alive in them. The sentence rows for `person` and `none` are kept, with a bias set on the tuning photos so that at most 0.5% of them are called `person` or `none`. How often a person is then called a person is unmeasured.

confidence.head: prototypes + sentences
confidence.text: For the head `prototypes + sentences`, the scale was set on the tuning photos (expected calibration error 0.101 there). A species is named when its probability is at least 0.90, the lowest level from which named species were right at least nine times in ten on the tuning photos; three species are offered when the first three together reach 0.96, set the same way. On the test photos a species is then named for 14.4% (13.3 to 15.5) of photos and that name is right for 91.5% (89.2 to 93.7) of them; three species are offered for 5.9% (5.2 to 6.7) and hold the right one for 93.2% (90.4 to 96.0); 79.7% (78.4 to 80.9) get a kind of eye only. This table leaves out the page's rule that offers come from the winning kind; the section on shipping applies it.
